instruction:
This is a fully open-workflow engineering task. You may use any tools, scripts, or libraries available in the environment, in any combination and any order, with any amount of iteration. The environment starts from a blank base image with no engineering applications preinstalled. Inspect the supplied inputs, then choose, install, and configure any tools or libraries you need. No particular software is required. The evaluator does not inspect software identity, stage order, intermediate handoffs, command history, version records, or provenance.

GNSS antenna keepout enclosure design.

Start from the supplied `board_input.kicad_pcb`, `design_requirements.json`, and `connector_keepouts.csv`. These files define the authoritative PCB geometry, installed coordinates, package dimensions, materials, tolerances, keepouts, and access bounds. They constrain the final design but do not prescribe a software workflow.

Use the PCB outline center as package XY origin and the tray bottom outer face as Z=0 without rotating or mirroring KiCad X/Y. Build the specified 95.4 x 95.4 x 35.4 mm ASA-UV package as a tray ending at Z=32.6 plus a separate 2.7 mm lid beginning at Z=32.7, preserving the 0.1 mm assembly separation. The inner cavity must be X=-45..45 and Y=-45..45. Seat the 1.2 mm PCB bottom at Z=16.8 on four 14.1 mm high bored standoffs aligned to MH1-MH4, using 6.4 mm outer diameter and 3.0 mm bore diameter, and preserve 4 mm clearance to every inner side wall. J1 ends at Z=25.2, leaving 7.5 mm to the lid inner face.

Keep J1 externally accessible through the bounded 24 x 8.8 mm X_PLUS wall window with cutter `[44.5, -24.0, 17.2, 48.2, 0.0, 26.0]` and enclosure-free path `[35.0, -24.0, 17.2, 48.2, 0.0, 26.0]`. Keep TP1 accessible through the 6 mm diameter Z_PLUS top bore with lid cutter `[15.0, -33.0, 32.2, 21.0, -27.0, 35.9]` and path `[15.0, -33.0, 18.2, 21.0, -27.0, 35.9]`. Bounds use `[xmin, ymin, zmin, xmax, ymax, zmax]`; both paths must be continuous through the relevant wall or lid and neither aperture may become a full-height or full-width slot. Apply the specified overcut, center/axis tolerances, and minimum access guard.

A1 requires a reserved air volume, not an exterior opening. Preserve the finite radius-24 cylinder centered on the KiCad A1 axis `(0, 16)` from A1 body top Z=23.2 to lid inner face Z=32.7, with bbox `[-24.0, -8.0, 23.2, 24.0, 40.0, 32.7]`. The nonconductive lid may cover it. Carrier material and non-A1 components may each intersect the reserved volume by no more than 0.1 mm3, and it must retain 5 mm radial clearance to the cavity wall. Extra structural features are allowed only when the access, guard, board-clearance, antenna-reservation, and interference requirements remain valid.

The evaluator derives ASA-UV enclosure volume and mass from final submitted geometry and the specified density; do not assume a fixed expected mass. The evaluator also derives all four PCB side clearances, covered-component clearances to the nearest covering enclosure material over each component footprint, four standoff bore checks, J1 and TP1 access checks, A1 keepout clearance and intersection checks, and unintended interference.

Save the completed final assembly into `/home/user/Desktop/result` as exactly one non-empty STEP or STP file; the filename is unrestricted. The STEP assembly must contain the physical enclosure or carrier, lid where required, PCB, installed components, and task-specific physical features in their final coordinates. The PCB and installed components must remain identifiable physical parts rather than being fused into enclosure material; this is a final-assembly geometry requirement, not a prescribed workflow. Additional files are allowed but are not required. The evaluator grades only the final submitted geometry against the design contract. It does not grade which tools were used, their order, intermediate filenames, logs, reports, renders, or software identity.
